utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries announced. Therefore, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Weber? Oh, you're just waiting for the witness to come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dragicevic. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Weber will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you and to everybody else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, would you like the witness to have his statement before him or --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's fine for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we leave it as is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30926 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would like to return to the document we left off with yesterday. It is from the VRS Main Staff sector for morale, religious, and legal affairs. It is dated 19 November 1994. This is three days before you became the assistant commander in the SRK, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The subject of the document is entitled: "Directions on some current issues regarding public information." These are directions from the Main Staff on how to inform the public, right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: These directions were sent to the sector for morale, religious, and legal affairs of the SRK, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, although there is something different in the typed text. It states Main Staff of the VRS as if it's typed on a different machine and then the type is different in the rest of the text but this is not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. When you became an assistant commander, you familiarised yourself with the Main Staff directions for your department; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived, first of all I was briefed by the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps about the general situation in the area of responsibility of the corps. And, of course, with -- he informed me about the elements of morale, his assessment of the current state of play with respect to morale in the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could listen to my carefully and if you could please focus very precisely on what I'm asking, did you familiarise yourself with the Main Staff directions that were in place for your department when you became an assistant commander in the SRK?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I provided you with a correct answer. If I were to go through this document, then I would be able to give you the answer with -- that you're after. Initially, I was briefed about the general state of affairs concerning morale in -- of the units in Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, to tell us that you gave the right answer, it may be true what you said but that's not an answer to the question. The question simply was: Did you familiarise yourself with the Main Staff directions that were in place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I were to read this document, I would be able to give a correct answer to your question. I gave my order about how things were. I do not know the content of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not talking about this document. We are talking about instructions given by the Main Staff previous to your arrival, whether you familiarised yourself with those directions, whether you, at the time, whether you familiarised yourself with them, irrespective of whether this one is included.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I understood what I was briefed about on the day when I arrived. Of course, later on I studied in greater detail those directions and other elements of morale and general guidance concerning the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to item 12, which is towards the lower portion on both pages. This direction states: "Mask our offensive activities maximally. Do not inform the public about these but in the advance stage present them as part of the natural right to self defence and a force response. In other words, a counteroffensive." This is an instruction by the Main Staff to intentionally misinform the public about VRS operations, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the text reads "do not inform the public." Well, this is, in terms of military way of doing things, why should the public be informed about military plans. Military plans are secret by their nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, that's not my question. And sorry to cut you off, but I'm going to start doing that a little bit more. My question to you was: This is an instruction by the Main Staff to intentionally misinform the public about VRS operations, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can understand, I see that it's not claimed here that public should be misinformed. It reads the public should not be informed about military operations before they take place. This is how I understand and read the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you take out one line of all of it and you apparently ignore that the text rather clearly states: "Give an image, present it in a way different from what it really is." Any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, of course, this is the basic rule. You have to conceal your plans about future military operations. This is rule number 1, so to speak. We are not going to inform the public about what we are about to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm happy to follow up on these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Here is how you discuss the activities of the SRK in your statement in this case. I'm going to read you a few passages here. In paragraph 22 you state: "The main goal of the army was to defend and protect the people" --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apologise. I do not have the text in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could have D554, paragraph 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And any problem if the witness would have a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be provided with a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, here is how you discuss the activities of the SRK in your statement. In paragraph 22, you state: "The main goal of the army was to defend and protect the people who happened to be in VRS-controlled territory. Our strategy was not to occupy all of BiH but to defend those parts which ethnically belonged to the Serbian people." In paragraph 22, you also state: "The strategy of the SRK was to defend the living space of the Serbian people and to protect itself and other loyal citizens in the area of Sarajevo and Romanija." In paragraph 23, you state: "We knew that in the coming several months, we were to face a difficult period of an all-out Muslim offensive." Paragraph 24, you state: "We knew what we were defending and it gave us incredible strength." Just to give one more example. In paragraph 34, you state: "Our fighters knew what they were defending. They were defending their homes and families and they knew they would have to sacrifice their lives in order to be successful." In all these statements, you are presenting the SRK's activities as part of a right to self defence, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You are not describing the strategy of the VRS or SRK as offensive at all.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you cannot have self defence without some offensive operations to gain certain positions which -- to make the self defence of the territory and the people effective. It doesn't -- this was not an offensive to -- with the aim of taking the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Offensive operations were taken to gain positions which would allow us to implement our strategy of defending the territory. We had to carry out certain offensive operations to improve our tactical or operational positions, but the essence of the strategy was defensive. It was not our intention to occupy all of Bosnia-Herzegovina and subjugate other peoples but to defend the right of the Serbian people to live, continue living freely in the territories that they had inhabited for centuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. So do I understand that you're basically saying that what the VRS was doing was a counteroffensive to defend themselves?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. If somebody carried out offensive operations or threatened certain areas belonging to the Serb people, of course. It was our mission, our task, to capture those territories --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, sir --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and put them under our control and liberate that part of the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could just answer my question. You answered it, I believe, right out of the gate there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 30926 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30926 receives number P6646, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yesterday, at transcript page 23703, you acknowledged that you issued work guidelines to subordinate units and to your own department. How often would you issue these work guidelines?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever I estimated and/or the command estimated that I was given a task to do so, this happened relatively often. There was no rules about them, unlike reports which had to be regular. Guidelines would be issued whenever the situation necessitated or whenever a superior officer demanded that of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Would you issue guidelines more frequently to the subordinate commands or to your own department?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When acting in my capacity of assistant commander for morale, legal and religious affairs, and this was the most often the case, I would issue guidelines falling within that remit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Not sure you answered my question. Did you more frequently issue work guidelines to the subordinate commands or within your own department?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. Those guidelines would be issued to subordinated units. Within the department for morale, legal, and religious affairs I would issue guidelines on a daily basis. Whenever we got together, we discussed issues, current issues. We drew conclusions, and I issued requisite orders concerning the activities of my department.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you issued guidelines to all of the SRK brigades?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes, to all of them. In other subordinated units to the command of the S -- RSK [as interpreted], if there was a need to separate certain brigades or parts of brigades, this was done as well. This all depended on the situation on the ground. This dictated and informed who we addressed those guidelines to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The purpose of work guidelines was to instruct members of the SRK on how to improve morale, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the sections and organs for morale, religious, and legal affairs of the subordinated units. Those guidelines addressed them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just can I interrupt, Mr. Weber? Witness, at page 8, line 15, you are recorded as saying, the command of the RSK. Did you mean RSK or SRK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously it should read "SRK."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As a morale officer, it was your job to keep members of the SRK focused on the main objectives of the war effort of the VRS, true?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first and foremost I was in charge of preserving and building combat morale. This was my basic duty. And of course, I took the requisite measures based on that basic task, to achieve the goals that had been set to that department of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. And were these to keep members of the SRK focused on the objectives of the war effort of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes. They were aimed at making the members of the SRK and to accept the overall situation, and to explain to them why they should conduct themselves in the way it was described in the directions and guidelines and that all of these things had a purpose and an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30902.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Colonel, these are the SRK command notification and guidelines for the work of the organ for moral guidance dated 2 December 1994. The document contains strictly confidential number 12/2-252. These guidelines are type signed from you. This particular copy of the guidelines was certified as true by Captain Bajic who yesterday you said that you believed to be the assistant for morale of the Ilijas Brigade. Is it correct that this document relates to your organ of the SRK command?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although it is not very well visible, I believe this is so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We can see that -- we can all see that this document deals with a few different things, but I would like to focus your attention to the fifth paragraph of these work guidelines, where you wrote: "Our task is to strengthen the combat morale of our soldiers and officers and to build up confidence in our capabilities and in the excellence of Serbian arms. Yes, we are genetically stronger, better, more handsome, and cleverer. Try to remember how many Muslims there were among top ten pupils, students, or soldiers. Only a few. Why? Because they are poturice and only the weakest of the Serbs became poturice." My question: Do you acknowledge that this is derogatory language?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Basically this is all true and confirmed my previous experience. Life experience. Since I am interested in biology I know that the phylogenesis and genetic mutation is something that stems from it. I stand by all of it. Of course, there is a bit of propaganda here as well --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- as it is one of the ways to build up combat morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to go through each sentence with you but right now I'd like to stop. I looked up the definition of racism in the Oxford Dictionary which said -- which defined it as: "The belief that all members of each race possess characteristics, abilities, or qualities specific to that race. Especially so as to distinguish it as inferior or superior to another race or races." Sir, based on this definition, you are a racist, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object to counsel testifying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object to counsel testifying. And if he's talking about race, this appears to be talking about people of the same race and according to the common definition of that term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, where does counsel testify, Mr. Ivetic? I think he gave the basis for his question. He said what he found in a dictionary as the meaning of an expression and that he wants his question to be understood in accordance with that meaning of that word.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, during the case of the Prosecution, every time we tried to present something we had to present it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- on the screen as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- so the issue is that you say it's not in that -- it should be established by putting that dictionary --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If that's the case, you can perhaps leave the question for later if that's what Mr. Ivetic considers there should be doubts about, then we should accept that. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if counsel can also please just quickly look up the Oxford Dictionary definition of racism, I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Counsel is right that it's up for you to do that. However, if you would have phrased the question not referring to that specific dictionary, you could have phrased the question exactly the same way and then you would not have testified, you would have explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we would have saved five minutes and it also more or less indicates that it's perhaps a bit of a non-issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You already answered the question that I had. So I'd like to go through the statements in this paragraph a little bit more. You say: "Yes, we are genetically stronger, better, more handsome and cleverer." You are talking about people of Serb ethnicity, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My life experience confirms it and I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You believe that you are genetically more handsome than people of the Islamic faith?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that my experience confirms it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So that's a yes, that's what you believe?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. If I didn't, I wouldn't have written it. I do like to stress that there is some degree of calculated propaganda so as to build up our soldiers' morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We will come to what you just said in a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I first try to find out the following. In English, we read: "Yes, we are genetically stronger, better, more handsome and cleverer." Now, you can read that in two different ways. The first is we are genetically stronger, we are better, we are more handsome; and the other way of reading it is, yes, we are genetically stronger, genetically better, and genetically more handsome. Now, which of the two? Do you say that being better and more handsome is also genetically defined?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I think exactly the same way as it is stated. The genetic part refers to the adjective stronger, but I don't have the text before me and I'm unable to follow. It refers to the first term, not the whole phrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then may I advise you to more carefully listen to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The problem is not in listening. The problem is in me not seeing. It's too small. Could we zoom in on the passage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you can't see the question on the screen so it's also a matter of listening. Could we enlarge the relevant portion of the -- which is approximately in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Paragraph 5. But we move the English for a short moment. And then enlarge paragraph 5, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the translation shows some ambiguity I wonder whether the original text also does so. That's not -- and I would like to have that verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We had this document actually verified so the text was as it is -- appears in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to hear from the Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- currently available translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to hear from the Defence whether they consider the original as ambiguous as the translation. Please proceed for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is blatantly racist language, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say, "Try to remember how many Muslims there were among the top ten pupils, students or soldiers," you're not just talking about Muslim soldiers here, right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers too. You can see it nicely. The question is also how many soldiers there were among the rest. I worked as an officer, and I know that I trained soldiers of many ethnicities and this was a conclusion of mine based on experience again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is not limited to soldiers, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But it does include them as well. It's precisely as it's stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You, as a senior officer, could you tell us what impact this language would have on members of the SRK? Particularly young recruits who were new to the army? What was your intended effect of this?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basic goal was to build up combat morale, and to have the -- to make the officers and soldiers have faith in themselves so that they grow in self-confidence, confident of their own ability.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I take it from your testimony today that you find this to be a perfectly acceptable way of trying to build up this morale in the soldiers of the SRK?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These instructions were intended first and foremost for the officers working on the issues of morale and religious affairs in subordinate units. Given the situation in the field, this was not merely a theoretical position. It was dictated by the situation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and among other ways --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- we tried to build up self-confidence in this way too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The simple question was whether you considered this to be an acceptable way of achieving what you said was your task. And I take it from your answer that you just say yes in your view this was an acceptable way. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The language is acceptable. Perhaps the choice of words is not the best one, but I did mention that there are elements of propaganda therein. If we were to discuss it whether it was scientific and 100 per cent correct I'd rather not go into it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you've explained that. But you considered it acceptable under the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please move on, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Going back to paragraph 22 of your statement in this case, you state that the VRS strategy was "to defend those parts which ethnically belong to the Serbian people." You still view the actions of the VRS as being justified because of your Serb ethnicity today, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you still view the actions of the VRS as being justified by your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fail to understand at all. What is it that you're asking of me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is not very clear, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please, because it's a rather complex matter you are addressing at this moment, and I think the witness is right in asking you to do it in a more elaborate way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your statement, when you say "to defend those parts which ethnically belong to the Serbian people," you are saying that the actions of the VRS were justified because of Serb ethnicity, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm still trying to grasp the meaning of the question. If you have in mind whether our offensive actions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, I invited you not to repeat the question in a different way but --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was trying to work through your directions. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You failed to do that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right. If we could go to the next paragraph on the -- if we could return, actually, to the document we were looking at on the screen, which was 65 ter 30902.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, I'd like to go to the paragraph that follows. It's actually just one sentence that follows the paragraph we were looking at. So this is approximately the sixth from the top. The paragraph states: "A solid and well thought out punch in the nose would make them change their faith once again." When you were referring to changing their faith, you are referring to the "poturice," as you describe them, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, are you saying that religious conversion justified the actions of the SRK?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that. I'm saying that they frequently changed faith, and ethnicity even. Hence, I drew the conclusion that it would be easy for them to do so again, to move on to the next faith or ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And as a person in morale, is it correct that you were seeking to encourage a solid and well-thought-out punch on the nose in order to accomplish this?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During a previous period while I commanded a brigade in Visegrad, I have to say, at the risk of being immodest, I never suffered any defeat. I always came out victorious and it was precisely that that I based my experience on. This information covers that experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, again you haven't answered my question. Is it correct that you were seeking to encourage a solid and well-thought-out punch on the nose in order to accomplish this, this conversion?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. In that way, I wanted to encourage those I was addressing; i.e., the subordinate commands and units. The basis of my statements is in my previous experience. I knew how one needs to wage a fight against them to be successful, against members of the ABiH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just try to avoid that there is a basic misunderstanding. Apparently, Mr. Weber reads "well-thought-out punch on the nose" to be inflicted upon the poturice so that they would change their faith once again, and I must say that sounds at least rather logic. In your answer you're saying you are addressing your own subordinates. But could you please tell us what you meant in your answer? You said you wanted to encourage those I was addressing, it is the subordinate commands and units. It looks as if you're addressing them to inflict the well-thought-out punch on the nose to the "poturice," to encourage the "poturice" to change their faith again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The last part is incorrect. This is what I wanted. It was my previous experience that I wanted to convey to the people I was addressing in order to encourage them and to tell them that no great effort was needed. They only needed to be decisive and believe in achieving victory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it reads, for -- I'd say for many perhaps, that you say, "Well, some force will be enough to make them change their faith again," "them" being the "poturice." Is that misunderstood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether they would change faith, but no one would be forcing them to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you would use force with a certain aim, isn't it? That's what the line is about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was directed towards achieving combat success and the best possible results. That is the meaning of this entire paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We've heard your explanation. Please move on, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 30902 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30902 receives number P6647, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6647 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would like to change topics. In paragraph 2 of your statement, you indicate that you were the chief of staff and then commander of the Visegrad Brigade in 1992. Is it correct that the Visegrad Brigade was part of operations group Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During what? The term "Operations Group Podrinje" is something I'm not aware of, but do be more specific in terms of period. I've never heard of an operations group Podrinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P3677 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a VRS Main Staff order to set up Operations Group Podrinje dated 14 July 1992 from General Mladic. We know this is a few days before you took up your position. In the first paragraph of this order, there are references to two meetings that were held on 7 and 11 July 1992. Before we move on, I just want to simply ask you: Did you attend either of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And it is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of the B/C/S and page 2 of the English translation. I'm going to be focusing on item 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Colonel, directing your attention to item 4 which discusses the setting up of Tactical Group Gorazde. In this section General Mladic indicates that the 2nd Podrinje Lpbr is to be composed of certain units. Before we discuss these units, is it correct that your brigade in 1992 was the 2nd Podrinje Lpbr?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this order, your brigade is to be composed of battalions and manned with the available forces in the Visegrad and Rudo municipalities. When you took over your position or when you assumed your position in July 1992, who were the forces that were available to man VRS battalions from the Visegrad municipality?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the point of my arrival, the brigade was based on companies. The purpose of this order, in my view, was to make command easier because it was difficult to command the units spread all over that large territory. Although I had never seen this order, nevertheless I implemented it once I became brigade commander. The situation dictated that there was a reorganisation of the brigades in this manner. However, there is one thing that is not clear. The Visegrad Brigade was based on personnel from the Visegrad municipality rather than from Rudo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I want to be clear about this. Is it correct that the 1st Visegrad Light Infantry Brigade was incorporated into the 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The initial title was the Visegrad Brigade. It was later changed to become the 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade. It is the same unit. However, it was -- there was a change of name and establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think generally we are talking about the same thing, but just to be clear, was -- the initial Visegrad Brigade, that was commanded by Vinko Pandurevic, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You also incorporated volunteers from Serbia, right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, but I wanted to explain the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We as the brigade could not take anyone in. Someone had to have been mobilised and sent to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, we will go through this and if we can do it in an orderly fashion. I'll keep my questions simple. The way that the Serb volunteers were incorporated into your brigade was through the SJB, the police station in Visegrad, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It went through the military secretariat. The SJB was included in the part of the process which had to do with the screening of those people arriving, based on their own procedures related to security, et cetera. The military secretariat accepted such volunteers who had gone through the screening process with the SJB. They would make sure they had served their military term and did their part of the job. Then they would mobilise them and such people would receive a draft call which they needed to bring to the brigade. The brigade received such people. It couldn't take anyone in directly, otherwise it would have been unlawful and it could not be done without the previous checks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were members of the SJB Visegrad, so the policemen themselves, conscripted into your brigade?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Police is a separate segment. They functioned separately from us. Of course, there was cooperation concerning the situation on the ground, but they themselves were not members of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did the members of the SJB Visegrad participate in VRS operations?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Of course. There would be a request sent to their superior order -- organs, and if that request was resolved in a positive manner, they, if needed, would take part in operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see we are at time for a break. I was about to move on for a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we take it right now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if this is a suitable moment for the break. We'll ask the witness to follow the usher and be back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, aside from the groups that we discussed already, were there any other groups that were incorporated into the 2nd Podrinje Brigade? Specifically in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, no. If you could be more specific, then I could be more specific in my answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were there any Bosnian Serb volunteer groups, as I believe how you would consider them, that were already existing prior to July 1992 that were incorporated into your brigade?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already explained how one could become member of this brigade. There was no other way except if a regular unit of the VRS would come to help us out. But specifically, there was no other way to incorporate any other groups into the brigade --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in that period that I spent there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to cut you off because you're explaining to me a process. My question was factual in nature. Were there any Bosnian Serb volunteer groups that were existing prior to July 1992 that were incorporated into your brigade?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of any such thing. It was impossible for anybody to enter the brigade except through going through a process -- the process that I explained to you sometime ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do I understand correctly that your answer today is no, there were no Bosnian Serb volunteer groups incorporated into your brigade?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. In a way where a group would come to the brigade and the brigade would accept it. No. Individuals had to be mobilised through the mobilisation section, to be issued with draft calls, and then they would be deployed in specific units. In July, the brigade had only companies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I try to cut matters short. Were individuals incorporated which were known to have been before they were incorporated to be a group of volunteers, even though admitted individually?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the procedure is the same. Nobody could enter a brigade without --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Don't repeat your previous answers. Were -- in accordance with the procedure you already described, were individuals incorporated which were known to have formed a group before they were incorporated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about that. That's possible, but the mobilisation centre would determine who would go into which brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you testified before the high court in Bijelo Polje Montenegro on 19 February 2002?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the year, but it is true that I testified before a high court in Bijelo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In that case you testified to events that related to the abduction of over 20 Muslim men at the Strpci train station in Rudo on 27 February, 1993. That's what the case was about, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During that testimony, did you take an oath to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was that oath similar to the one you took before your testimony in this case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- how many different oaths you are aware of to tell the truth and different -- a bit of the truth or all of the truth? I mean, it's a useless question, unless there is any specific reason to put it to the witness if you have any reason to believe that these oaths are different from what they are everywhere else in the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your testimony before the high court in Montenegro, is it correct that you discussed your time as a commander in the Visegrad Brigade and those who were under your command?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I testified about the period while I was brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you aware that Milan Lukic has been convicted before this Tribunal for crimes committed against the Muslim population of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object, beyond the scope of the indictment. Visegrad is not in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This goes to the witness's credibility, and I'm just asking if he was aware of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you aware that Milan Lukic has been convicted before this Tribunal for crimes committed against the Muslim population of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I learned it from the media, about the judgement that was handed down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30929 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you is the trial record of your testimony in February 2002 before the high court. I'm going to go through a number of statements that you made during these proceedings. While we go through these statements, I may have a few additional questions. After I go through these statements we will discuss some material related to the statements that you made. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood. I hope I will be able to see what I had testified about concerning the gist of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the B/C/S and page 3 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: First, I would like to discuss what you said about the composition of your brigade. Toward the middle bottom part of the page before you, the trial record states: "The brigade was made up of companies. It included an intervention company. Boban Indjic from Visegrad was the commander of this intervention company until he was wounded, when Rade Tanovic came." First, do you see this portion?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this was your testimony about your brigade and Boban Indjic?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm all the text that you read out loud.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Toward the bottom of the same page, you are recorded as stating: "I knew Milan Lukic of Visegrad by sight. And I know that he was neither a member of my brigade nor a soldier."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have the next page of the B/C/S original for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It continues: As far as I know he was in prison in Uzice and Belgrade during the time I was brigade commander. I do not know anything about his activities in the Visegrad area." Can you confirm that this was your testimony about Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this testimony, you say that you knew Milan Lukic by sight. Where would you see him?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, specifically, the first time I saw him was in town. I very rarely went through town because I had no time for that. I was in a car. The driver pointed out him -- pointed him to me. It was in town in front of a cafe that he owned. He was standing in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. You said that was the first time. When was it?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe late autumn. It was quite cold, very cold, foggy, frosty. Could be the end of 1992 or the beginning of 1993. I can't be more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. How often would you see Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During combat operations in Visegrad, in other words while I was brigade commander, and after that head of -- chief of the tactical group, very rarely. I can't really recall whether I saw him any other time. I remember that he was wearing not military-issue camouflage fatigues. It looked more like a police-issue fatigues, white and grey stripes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We will come back to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 5 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the third paragraph on the page before you, this is also in the upper portion of the page of the translation, you are recorded as stating: "There were two volunteer platoons. In military operations, these platoons were attached to the intervention company. I know that they had official designations as our units but perhaps the soldiers had other slang names for them. I heard some of the names used by the soldiers such as Osvetnik, Garavi Sokak, and that that was what they used to call each other. However, none of the units had official names like these." Can you confirm that this was your testimony before the high court?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You refer to the Osvetnik and Garavi Sokak in this statement. Isn't it correct that these were groups of Bosnian Serb volunteers who existed in Visegrad that then came under your brigade's command?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all -- not all conscripts could be volunteers from the area of Visegrad. They were mobilised and they cannot by definition be volunteers if they come from Visegrad, if they are conscripted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. These groups -- individuals from these groups were conscripted into your brigade, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether those were groups or not. I never dealt with that problem. But at any rate, people who did -- who had done their military service, military term, they were conscripted and mobilised into the Visegrad brigades and which later on became 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. We will come back to these groups. At the end of this page you stated in response to a question concerning whether smaller units from the Visegrad Brigade could carry out operations without you knowing. You stated: "A unit could not carry out any military operation as a unit without my knowledge." Was this your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object, Your Honours. If he's going to quote the testimony, he's going to have quote the same -- the whole testimony, not take one sentence and stop there and say that's the whole testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I take this to be an invitation for Mr. Weber to give a larger quote than he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I was just merely putting the fact to him. But if you want me to read the question and the answer I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The trial record states: "Asked by the prosecutor whether one of the small units from the Visegrad Brigade could carry out a military operation without him knowing about it, the witness replied: "'A unit could not carry out any military operation as a unit without my knowledge.'" Was that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the answer continues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, something for re-examination, I think. Unless -- Mr. Weber, I have not read what follows. If that sheds a totally different light on it, then of course it's a bit narrow-minded to just put a thing where you know that later the other part will be put to the witness. I have not read it. Mr. Ivetic, you know what the remedy is. And Mr. Weber is reminded that that doesn't make much sense. Again, I haven't read it so I have no opinion about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, that was your testimony before the high court, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is how I testified. I commanded my subordinated units, not platoons which are lower level but the two battalions and the intervention company and staff units. These were my direct, immediate subordinates, and I commanded over them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 8 of the B/C/S and page 7 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you do agree that you were asked in that proceedings about smaller units and you didn't make any distinction between platoons or battalions? You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not fully understand you, but what I can tell you is that I commanded directly the subordinate units which are battalion level and the intervention company which was part of the brigade by establishment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was asking you about the testimony you gave in those other proceedings, not about what happened on the ground. But if you don't understand it, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At the very beginning of this page --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is near the top of the page of the translation also.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- the trial record records you as stating: "I was also informed about the other abduction which occurred in Sjeverin through the media as well, just as I was about this Strpci case." Can you confirm that this is what you said?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask you about your awareness of this other abduction. Are you aware that the Sjeverin abduction occurred on 22 October 1992, and it involved the taking of 16 Muslims from Sandzak, 15 men and one woman who were riding a bus, that these individuals were abducted in the village of Mioce [phoen] and taken to Visegrad where they were never seen again? Are you aware of these facts?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about this. I learned from the media about these facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you testified before the high court, were you aware that Milan Lukic was a suspected perpetrator for both the Sjeverin and Strpci abductions?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I learned of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before I test the truthfulness of some of the statements that you've confirmed from the high court, I'd also like to ask you: Are you aware that Milan Lukic was arrested on unrelated gun possession charges four days after the Sjeverin abduction, precise date being 26 October 1992?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was arrested and I learned, of course, that the reason for the arrest was possession of weapons. But I can't remember the time. I believe it was in November/December 1992, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to go through some materials related to this arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30932 for the witness. The Prosecution requests that this document not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a Republic of Serbia State Security Service Uzice Centre Official Note dated 2 November 1992. In the first line of this document, it indicates the source of the information is Milan Lukic, the leader of the Osvetnici group. During your 2002 testimony in Montenegro, this was the group that you said was attached to the intervention company of your brigade, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, misstates the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It does, Mr. Weber. I think the witness testified that people were incorporated which were called, although not officially named, as the Avengers. But that they were called that, although it wasn't their official name. But that -- but --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I dis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you read --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I disagree because I read him his quote from his state court testimony which said: "In military operations these platoons were attached to the intervention company..." And he went on to say that they used slang names for them including the names Osvetnik and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which suggests that it's the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but which has not been established yet. To that extent it misrepresents. Although it's on a detail, I'm aware of that. But the more precise your language, the more you'll avoid these kind of objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the group that you referred to in your high court testimony, correct, the Osvetnik?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified before the high court that the soldiers would call one another in their argot different names. Specials, poison, avengers. These were internal nicknames. This is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you stating that you heard of the group Osvetnik?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear about the group Avengers, but what I said here and what I said at -- before the high court, this I maintain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to just show you a little bit of -- have you look at a little bit of information before we move on to another part of this report. According to this Official Note, this interview of Milan Lukic occurred on 26 October 1992 after he was stopped at a check-point in Serbia and found to be in possession of weapons. Do you see this information on the page before you?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before I move on, I just want to note for the record the weapons because we will come back to them later. These weapons included a Thompson submachine-gun, a 7.62 millimetre rifle, hand grenades, and a 7.65 millimetre pistol, according to the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have page 2 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the middle of the page, Milan Lukic is recorded as stating: "I participated in all important military operations in the Visegrad area. This was a real interethnic war and I came to the front with only one goal: To protect Serbs and Serbdom in this area. Since the arrival of Vinko Pandurevic, I was under his command, in legal units of Republika Srpska." Before I move on to another statement, do you see this part of the document before you?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Toward the top of this page, Milan Lukic is recorded as stating: "In Visegrad, I found a bad situation, a small numerical strength, low morale with commander Luka Dragicevic and commander of the Tactical Group 1, Vinko Pandurevic, who was at the Rudo front together with Lieutenant-Colonel Mitrasinovic." Based on these statements, is it correct that Milan Lukic was in fact part of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He never was. I never heard of his individual participation in any brigade command activity. He couldn't have because he was not a member of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We are going to go through some more documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 30932 into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. During the Prosecution case whenever we tried to use statements of third parties not brought as witnesses, Your Honours said you have to bring the persons to attest to the statement. This is a statement. Therefore we object. The Prosecution cannot enter this document for the truth of the matter asserted in this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you make any distinction between different kinds of statements? If it was a statement taken for the purposes of proceedings before this Tribunal, certainly you're right. Now, did we always insist on that if statements were taken for other purposes? And if so, could you please assist us in pointing at the decisions we took in that respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd have to ask some time review the record. I can't recall the transcript page off the top of my head, but I could at the break look for it. So if we could then mark for identification and perhaps resolve the matter and wait for the submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection pending, Madam Registrar, could you assign a number so that we can mark for identification this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30932 receives number P6648, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30934, page 3 of the B/C/S and page 4 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up before you is the criminal report related to Milan Lukic's arrest on 26 October 1992. I'm just showing you this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we enlarge it? I can't see it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just out of an abundance of caution, based on what Ms. Stewart just informed me, if we could not have it broadcast for the time being. Thank you, Ms. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just showing you this document before we move on to another document so you see the serial numbers of the weapons - in particular, the serial number for the Thompson, which is 91053; and the serial number for the 7.65 millimetre pistol, which is K315414. This criminal report also indicates there were four grenades. Do you see this information, before we move on?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution now please have 65 ter 08519, page 2 in both versions. And, Your Honours, I plan on tendering this document with the next one. If I could please have the next page of both versions. I believe it's the other page of the B/C/S. I do not believe we have the correct page of the B/C/S on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have -- or isn't it? No, perhaps not all of it, but I see number -- let's have a look. Perhaps it's partly here and partly on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is this page 1 or page 2 in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look. We have the various --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, page 1 in the B/C/S. If we could have that. Here we go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it's the same form but filled in. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a receipt for weapons received by Milan Lukic dated 28 September 1992, almost a month before his arrest. At the bottom we see that this receipt contains the stamp of the army of the republic of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Visegrad command. And the serial numbers of the Thompson and the pistol match the ones in the criminal report we just looked at. There is also reference to hand grenades. I put it to you that the Visegrad command supplied Milan Lukic with weapons.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that position of yours. But the logistics person at the command could confirm it or deny. There is a problem with the date, though, because it seems to have been changed, the 28th of September 1992. I think originally it was a different month, and then it was changed. This is what I can see at a first glance. There is nothing else I can say about the document. I didn't issue it and I was not in command at the time. I don't know how it came about. You would need to ask those who had issued those weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a receipt. I don't think regular soldiers were issued against receipts -- issued with weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go through one more document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And actually I'll tender all three together. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 02555 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you are certificates from you, for Milan Lukic and Dragutin Dragicevic. According to the top certificate, Milan Lukic was engaged in units of the VRS in Visegrad from 19 May 1992 to the present. The stamp on the documents are the same as the ones we just saw on the weapons receipt. I put it to you that you have not been truthful about your knowledge of Milan Lukic and his association to your brigade and these certificates that I've just shown you demonstrate that. Do you have any comment?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I responsibly claim that you are incorrect. This is a fake document. First of all, I didn't sign it, although we can see my name printed. But please show me the date when this certificate was issued, and the place where there should be a date seems to have been covered. It's black.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So, sir, are you denying that these are your initials on the certificate by the signature line? I get it, it's type signed.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you could see from all other documents, I never initialled them. I signed them. It was the only signature I used and it was on my military ID when I was made 2nd Lieutenant; that is to say, an active officer. I have always used that signature, including the present. I never initialled it. This is obviously a fake certificate. If you show us the date --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, sir --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- you will be able to see for yourself. Please let me explain, if you want --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I do have more questions about it. Are you saying you do not recognise these initials?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I don't recognise them and the initials aren't mine. That is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were there occasions when people signed for you?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Show me the date of issue for this certificate, and I'll explain it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That wasn't my question, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that again and again. If it's a fake document, what would be the purpose of concealing the date? Can you explain that to me? Because you insist so much on it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. I insist upon it so as to make it clear for you. This is poor grammar as well. Somebody managed to get ahold of a form and obviously they didn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Stop. I'm stopping you there. You insist that looking at the date would clarify issues for us. First question I put to you: What is the -- what's the purpose of, if you want to make a fake document, to conceal it? Or is it a forged document; that is, that it is your signature but that the date has been removed which sheds then light on what you just told us? Which of the two: Is it entirely fake or is it changed as far as the date being taken off, taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is completely fake. The date is important because it needs to be compared with the stamp because the stamp changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I indicate that you should stop speaking because I have the next question. I have now an answer to my first question. You say it's a completely fake document. And then my question is: What is the purpose, if you create a fake document, to conceal a date? I would put -- on such a totally fake document, I would put on it the date which is most convenient to me. Could you tell us what the purpose of erasure of the date is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The purpose is obvious. These two appeared before a court, both. This document was created for the court so as to show before the court that they belonged to the VRS, whereas they did not. They were both sentenced in Belgrade. Let alone the fact that this was not filled out in a soldierly way. First of all, we did not have a reconnaissance sabotage platoon but we had a sabotage reconnaissance platoon. Next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That goes beyond my question. My question was what was the purpose of erasing the date. I've received an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question. Mr. Dragicevic, could you please tell us to what institution the stamp on this original belongs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you can see, on the stamp, this is the first stamp that was used, one can clearly see it reads: "The Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." Later on, we became the Army of Republika Srpska and the stamp was changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just on the notion of the stamp, that would have been the stamp that would have been used prior to that change, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. While that was the case, we used this stamp and this kind of template. But this form, this kind of certificates, could not have been issued for that purpose. Its purpose was different. It served to acknowledge that members of the army were in receipt of assistance, say, from the Red Cross or another organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In response to Judge Orie's question, you said this document was created for the court so as to show before the court that they belonged to the VRS. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified twice at the district court in Belgrade and I know of this document. These two appeared before the court and were sentenced, and it's quite clear that this kind of form was allegedly issued to them at the relevant time. It begs no further clarification. If there was a date, everything would be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's therefore your conclusion that it must have been produced for court purposes. Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm completely convinced, basically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the Uzice district court terminated the detention of Milan Lukic on 4 November 1992 because evidence was presented which indicated that Milan Lukic and the co-accused Dragutin Dragicevic were members of the Visegrad Brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it. Had he been a member of the army, we would have had that piece of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, he had not been and we never had that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please stop talking when I give you a clear sign to do so? You've answered the question, you're not aware of it. We are not seeking, unless specifically asked for that, your further elaborations. You're not aware of it. That answers the question. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm simply putting this to you, that you -- actually, your brigade issued this certificate for these individuals to secure their release back in late October, early November 1992. Do you have any other comments?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely untrue. It did not take place with my knowledge. I was even threatened with murder by the relatives of this Milan Lukic because they wanted me to issue a certificate of -- like that, and risking my life, I refused. He had not been mobilised, he was not a soldier, and not a member of the brigade. My life was under threat directly. I believe many others feared him, and that out of fear they may have been prone to issue fake certificates, although I'm not sure. That is my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. You've been claiming up till now that you did not have much knowledge, and then you just said: "I was even threatened with murder by the relatives of this Milan Lukic because they wanted me to issue a certificate...," when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened when he was in the Uzice prison, during that time. Their explanation was that if he were to receive an army certificate, it would be a mitigating circumstance because he had certain weapons illegally and that was what he was charged with.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to move on to some additional materials somewhat related to the topic. I can tender the three documents now or actually tender them with another two that I'm going to be using.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you then wait. Could you -- Mr. Weber, could you shed a bit more light on the provenance of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I can if we can do that -- [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Because I'm not asking you to do it now but before the Chamber will further consider admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, then could we have them all marked for identification. I believe with the other MFI, if we can just pool these together and then discuss them all at once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we could do so. Mr. Ivetic, I see you are apparently in agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I can read the 65 ter numbers if you'd like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you could do that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would be tendering 65 ter numbers 30934, 08519, and 039 -- excuse me --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: 02555. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30934 receives number P6649. Document 08519 receives number P6650. And Document 02555 receives number P6651, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All three marked for identification, under seal. Only the first one under seal, that is P6649. The others public documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I believe we are at a time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are. Witness, we take a break of 20 minutes. You may follow the usher, and we'd like to see you back at 10 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 10 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to alert the Chamber and the parties that I might not use the full day today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I might not need the last session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that Mr. Ivetic may need some time for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. At this stage probably 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So therefore there is a fair chance that we would conclude the testimony of this witness today, which is appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I guess while we're waiting, Your Honours, I can direct Your Honours to transcript page 18652 through 18654 in relation to a non-ICTY statement of an out of court person, 1D1370, which was denied admission in relation to the Prosecution case in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30936.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a report from the 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade dated 22 February 1993, from a deputy security commander, Captain Vucelja. At this time, were you the commander of this brigade?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This report indicates that there are no paramilitary formations or groups in the brigade but there are groups under the brigade command including the Osvetnik.
