After having seen this document, do you agree that the groups that are mentioned here were respecting your brigade's command?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've already explained. Soldiers addressed each other with these names that meant something to them, but among our formations there were no groups called this. There were platoons, companies, and later battalions, when the establishment was changed. It could only have been the 1st Platoon of the 1st Company or the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion and so on. As for the different names, they used all sorts of names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: These names that these individuals used, these are the names that -- the group names that they used, right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that. I don't know if they called each other those names individually or more of them accepted such nicknames. I really never bothered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I put it to you that this document shows -- also shows that Milan Lukic's group, the Osvetnik, were respecting your brigade's command. Do you have any comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, states facts not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Disagree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One second, please. What is not in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we have a discussion about this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, is it about the document not being in evidence yet? What -- what -- I do not fully understand your objection, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No. The --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for this discussion the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether it's -- if it's -- could you take off your ear-phones for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the witness said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the witness said he knows some English. Then could the leave the courtroom for a second and to remain standby.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said I don't speak English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Very limited from what I understand but nevertheless. Even in the English language, some issues might be raised which could be overheard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's not in evidence, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't believe it's in evidence -- and I just lost the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I can assist --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Milan Lukic's group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the Serbian DB report that we looked at, it started that Milan Lukic was leader of the group named the Osvetnik, so that is the basis of this. The witness has disagreed with it. I'm going through this line of cross-examination to test his credibility, and I'm confronting him - which is the way I phrased my question, that I put it to you - and I'm putting the proposition to him. I believe this is perfectly proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic, if you put something to a witness as a proposition then it doesn't need to be in evidence. As a matter of fact, you seek that to become evidence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But it doesn't say "I put it to you Milan Lukic...," it says "I put it to you that this document shows," this document being the one on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So we're mixing apples and pears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. It's the proposition that this document is indicative for what Mr. Weber says. Now, whether he's asking for a conclusion on the document, that's a different matter, would perhaps be a different objection, but Mr. Weber puts that to the witness. This document shows that. It's not in evidence. It's clear, what he seeks. As a matter of fact, he seeks the witness to draw conclusions which --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But this document does not mention Milan Lukic. That's my point. They're trying to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, doesn't need to do that. That's because it's about conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that -- could the witness be escorted back into the courtroom. It may go without saying but the objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, perhaps you again put to the witness what you wanted to put to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, drawing your attention back to the document, I put it to you that this document further shows that Milan Lukic's group, the Osvetnik, were respecting your brigade's command. Do you have any comment?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I can. It says here that those names could bring about an association or are reminiscent of existence of paramilitary groups. I also said that they called each other different names but group -- as a group could not have existed. There are 1st Detachment, 1st Platoon, 1st Company, 1st Battalion, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you are -- the one who reports here uses the expression "group," isn't it? All these groups. So he refers to them as groups. Have you any comment on that? And I see that in the original also the word "grupa" is used.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He used that term but there were no other groups. There are detachments, which are part of a platoon, platoon is a part of a company. How large were those groups? I don't know. But there were no groups as groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We've heard your explanation. Please move on, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the last answer you just used a pronoun, you said "he." Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 3096 -- 30936 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, I have one or two questions. Witness, do you know Captain Veselin Vucija?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I know him. He was, as it's stated here, assistant security -- or deputy security commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Of which unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us to what institution the stamp there on the original belongs to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not very legible. I can't make out anything except to establish that there is a rubber stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it any better now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can make out command of the 2nd Podrinje and the rest is illegible, but it's evident that this would be a command of the 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You tendered the document. I think we marked them for identification. Or is this a new series which is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is new series [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection to this one. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30936 receives number P6652, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6652 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 30933, page 1 of the original and page 2 of the translation. The Prosecution asks that this document not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, before you is another Serbian DB official note from the Uzice centre. This one is dated 4 March 1993 and it relates to the Strpci abduction on 27 February 1993. Directing your attention to the bottom of the page before you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Which I believe is on the next page of the translation. I think we've gone one page too far in the translation. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- there is a reference to -- there is actually multiple references to Boban Indjic who is described as the leader of the Garavi Sokak. And there is also references to a truck that was used or is associated with the Strpci train abduction. Do you see this information?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Boban Indjic that is referred to here is the one that you referred to in your previous high court testimony as being a part of your infantry -- intervention company?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was commander of the intervention company.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have the next page in the B/C/S for the witness before I ask my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I just wanted you to see the complete information. On this page of the report at the top, it indicates that a policeman from Rudo saw the truck proceeding along the route from Strpci after the abduction of the passengers on the train. According to this report, the policeman recognised Indjic as one of the people in the truck. Do you see this information?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could please specify whether it's towards the top or bottom or?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It should be at the very top of the page before you.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the next page? I have page 2 here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll refrain from stating the name of the individual, and if you could do the same --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- but if see a reference to a policeman from Rudo --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Have you read that first paragraph on this page?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. I looked for those family names. Am I supposed to read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I just want to give you an opportunity to read the paragraph before I ask you a question. The very top paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is no need to read it out loud but just to familiarise yourself with the names in there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's clear, yes, thank you. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you based on this information is simple. I put it to you that the men from your brigade participated in the Strpci abduction on the 27th of February 1993, based on this information. Do you have any comment?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this information, it seems to be so, judging by the name. And source of information is a policeman from Rudo. I'm not sure whether he would be the right person to be able to recognise anybody but I'm not going to dwell on that. But, however, I maintain that the brigade had nothing to do with this incident or abduction in Strpci, neither did it have such a crazy idea, neither did it have any plan, nor did it use any of its units for such an act. This would be an interstate problem and no sane commander would really want to go into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You just made a bunch of denials. Did you personally investigate whether or not men from your intervention company were involved in the Strpci abduction?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never received that kind of information before the trial, before the high court in Bijelo Polje. Only then, or sometime earlier from the press, I'd learned that one of the members of the brigade, a volunteer by the family name of Stojisavljevic, had been arrested initially reportedly because of smuggling, and then later on I found out that this was -- the reason was Strpci. But this was after the war. Only then did I learn that some members of the Visegrad Brigade had taken part in such crime. By that time, I was not in a position to take any action because the brigade had ceased to exist and I had left that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 30933 into evidence at this time under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30933 receives number P6653, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6653 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As under seal, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 02556. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade command report dated 21 October 1993 from a Major Pajevic. Is it correct that you were the Chief of Staff of the Visegrad tactical group at this time? You were no longer in this brigade specifically?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Let me point out one obvious --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, sir, I'm going to ask you about the document. If you could please wait.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, you are here to answer questions. If there is anything you would like to add to that, you may ask for my permission to do so. So then you address me and you just do not continue to speak out what you had on your mind. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, let's see if we address what's on your mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness would like address me --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and I gave him an opportunity to do so. What is there you want to address at this moment? And I add to that which cannot wait until later.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it is important. If you take a closer look, you see that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- he was a member of the brigade from -- well, the brigade did not exist at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, witness, witness, you had asked for permission, that is what. And I asked you what is there what could not be said at the end. Take a pencil, make it a little note if you want to, and at the end of your testimony you'll have an opportunity, if not already covered by the re-examination, and you'll be re-examined, and then you'll have an opportunity at the end to add anything which is relevant in relation to the questions that were put to you. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was the 2nd Podrinje Brigade part of the Visegrad tactical group?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after the Visegrad tactical group had been formed. But let me note that the tactical group is a temporary formation, the Visegrad Brigade or rather 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade was part of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I appreciate what you're saying. My next question would be: In October 1993, was the Visegrad -- was the 2nd Podrinje Brigade part of the Visegrad tactical group? Was the Visegrad TG in existence at that time?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the TG Visegrad did exist, but its competences lie primarily in coordinating combat operation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one asked you about the competences. In the answer to your previous questions you added already something Mr. Weber was about to ask you. Here, whether Mr. Weber is interested in competences, "yes" or "no," wait for the next question which you may now put to the witness, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to go through each part of this report with you. The first sentence of this report indicates that Milan Lukic's dad asked for a certificate confirming his participation in the brigade. Were you aware of this? That on the 21st of October 1993, Milan Lukic's dad asked for this certificate?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. By that time, I'd transferred to the staff of the tactical group. I was chief of staff. This document is something that Vojko Pajevic drafted and he can explain everything about that. At that time I was not part of the 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade. I held no post there. I was at the tactical group Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do I understand your simple answer then is you were not aware of Milan Lukic's asking -- father asking for a certificate on this date?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This report continues to state that Milan Lukic joined the brigade as a volunteer on 26 April 1992 and is still a member of it. However, he was in prison at the time of this report. Do you know what Milan Lukic was in custody for at this time?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your earlier high court testimony, you said you were aware that Milan Lukic was in custody. How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was aware about November and December 1992. Of course, I heard later that he was detained on several occasions, but I didn't know when or on what grounds. I knew about his detention in Uzice because I was directly in a way involved because I received threats corroborated by weapons and being asked to give a certificate about his membership in the brigade but he was not a member. He was not part of any platoon. And this is the basic document which testifies to somebody's membership in a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This document then indicates that Milan Lukic made a contribution in liberating Visegrad, and "the army grew to like him for being who he was. And they request his release so he could lead his company again." Based on this document from your former brigade that you were commander of, is it correct that you have not provided truthful testimony concerning your brigade's relationship with Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In no way could this be said, particularly because I was personally exposed to threats of death. This document in my opinion serves a purpose concerning Lukic but he was never a member of the brigade and by the same token he could not have been a commander of a company in that same brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you ever report or communicate the threats you received to your superiors?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because a security organ was present at the time and he may have informed the station -- the public security station because those people were civilians, those who threatened me were civilians, not military personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did your -- did you ever take any action, your brigade, to remove these civilians or individuals from your zone of responsibility, that were threatening you?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was within the purview of security organs or the police. But frankly speaking, I did not pay much attention to that. There were so many other duties concerning combat operations that it never crossed my mind. I suppose that I should have done something but I simply did not have the time for that, except for carrying out my basic duties and missions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 2556 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2556 receives number P6654, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to change topics now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- can we perhaps then briefly deal with the earlier objection that is about the admission of the statement given before the Court. Mr. Ivetic, you referred us to certain transcript pages and in relation to a certain document. Isn't it true that the situation there was that portions of that statement were read to the witness and that the person who had given the statement was on the list of witnesses to be called and that under those circumstances, where the Defence said that it was sufficient to have read out the relevant portions of the statement, the remainder of it to be irrelevant, that -- and also in view of the fact that the person who gave the statement would be called as a witness later on, that under those circumstances, you objected to admission, which leads me -- first of all, is that your recollection as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, it's not a witness I dealt with nor was I in the courtroom for that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I take it that if you take me to the transcript pages --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that you have read them yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have read them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And my recollection is that at that time we did not have a witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But was it announced that that person would be called as a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, I read that pretty clearly --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- that my colleague said -- my colleague said perhaps he'll be a witness or probably he'll be a witness, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So there was a fair chance that he would be called as a witness. Now, Mr. Weber, you've read the relevant portions of the statement before the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I mean if you do require submissions I would like to have an opportunity to actually look at the stuff associated with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we will further consider it. But you know at least the reference Mr. Lukic made. Let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe there were two inferences -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "I will probably bring that witness to our case," that's probability, but at least in that expectation and the relevant portions to have been read out to the witness, that altogether led to a denial of the objection. That's the circumstances. Mr. Weber, perhaps you consider that and see whether that would need you to read other portions of the statement to the witness. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll fully respond at a time where I'm fully informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But please keep this in the back of your mind in continuation of your cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, just for the record, though, we do believe that the document itself is properly admissible and does not constitute a statement that in the fact of what counsel is describing. So I'll fully respond later, but just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll later hear them from you. For the time being, please proceed with as you said you would tackle a new area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P4439.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, coming up before you is the SRK combat readiness report dated 23 June 1994, at the bottom, and I believe the date 29 June 1994 appears at the top. I know this document is from before your time in the corps command, but I want to go through a few portions of it to see what you're aware of before you became a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This combat readiness reports starts with an introduction by the SRK commander. In June of 1994, were you aware that this was Stanislav Galic?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about this information that he was a commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, but I never knew him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to go through some of what is said here. In the second paragraph, that's before you, the report states: "Looking back on the past 27 months, I would say that not one day had gone by without combat (either defence or in attack) and measures being taken to control the territory and secure the facilities. As far as the implementation of the tasks set for us in the Main Staff VRS, Directives 1 through 6, this corps has executed all its tasks with a varying degree of success." Before I read the next paragraph, I just want to ask you: As a commanding officer, were you aware of Directives 1 through 6?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. The next paragraph starts: "The following can be viewed as success. The unwavering blockade of the Muslim part of Sarajevo and the prevention of frequent attempts of the de-blockading both from within the city out and from outside the city in." And then there is further details about operations. Were you aware of this information prior to becoming an assistant commander in the SRK?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you have in mind all of this? I wasn't aware of it. I said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's ask for a very simple thing. Were you aware that there was an unwavering blockade of the Muslim part of Sarajevo before you became a member of the SRK?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I knew that the SRK blocked the 1st Corps of the ABiH, which used most of Sarajevo as its base to engage the SRK. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you saying that you first learned this when you joined the SRK or you knew this before you became an assistant commander in the SRK?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I became assistant commander, then I learned of it, of course, and I could see it myself because I went in the field to find out the truth. I saw it personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just while we're on this page, if you could just read it and let me know if you know anything about the -- if you knew anything about the operations that are mentioned in this paragraph. Just "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew. I had information about these operations, but as the officer. I think I was still in Visegrad at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In fact, operation Lukavac 93 which is mentioned here involved the Drina Corps, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You participated in this operation?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This was an offensive operation, correct? It sought to liberate territory.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The goal was to liberate Serb areas which had been occupied. In order to conduct the operation, we needed to traverse certain parts that were controlled by the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You do not mention this operation in your statement, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 7 of the B/C/S and page 10 of the English translation? Your Honours, and just to inform the Court, I believe that there is a translation error in the portion that I'll be reading. The word "blokadi" has been translated as "siege," but I believe it should be "blockade." I just wanted to give everyone a heads-up on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As always, the parties' knowledge of what the translation should have been, that may be a reason for you to resubmit it --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to CLSS and not to bring your own interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I always tell all parties. If there's any doubt it should be verified by and if need be corrected by CLSS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And we are doing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But already I do understand for present purposes that you think that there may be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that we therefore should carefully look at the original language. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you is the part of the combat analysis where the SRK reports on its own situation. I'd like to direct your attention to the bottom portion of the page before you which is also towards the bottom in the translation. The paragraph states: "What we cannot present through numbers and which has a crucial effect on the situation in the units are the assessments showing the morale of units to still be at the satisfactory level which is also confirmed through facts that Sarajevo is successfully held under...," and this is the word, in the translation it says "siege," in the B/C/S I believe the word is "blokadi," "... and all of the more important tasks were carried out successfully." When you became an assistant commander in the SRK, did you assess the morale of the soldiers in the SRK in a similar way as this? Which is based on whether or not -- which appears to be based on whether or not they successfully held Sarajevo under blockade?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I carried out assessments, to the extent possible. I was aware that the war had been underway for over three years by the time I reached the SRK, and that the units and commands encountered numerous problems. Because of its duration it had a significant impact on the personnel. However, through work conducted by assistant commander for morale, we tried and succeeded, as confirmed by our victory in their latest offensive, to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- convince the people that despite those problems we had to soldier on, and we succeeded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if I can just interrupt you, in your assessments, did you assess the morale of SRK members based on whether they successfully held Sarajevo under blockade?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was whether they were successful in implementing their combat tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. And if their combat tasks included keeping Sarajevo held under blockade that would have been one of those tasks, right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Holding the 1st Corps of the ABiH under blockade was one of the predominant tasks of the SRK. It was not to hold Sarajevo under blockade, because a part of Sarajevo was under our control.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P6523 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you is an order with conclusions and tasks dated 1 April 1994 from General Galic. In the beginning paragraph of the document, there is reference to Operation Zvijezda, excuse me if I pronounce it, 94, which the SRK was taking part in with the Herzegovina Corps and the Drina Corps. Did you participate in this operation?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did, but I'm not sure what is understood by Star 94? Yes, yes, I did take part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could then go down to the second paragraph, there is a reference to forces and combat equipment which "on the request and per agreement of the Chief of Staff and commander of Visegrad TG." You were the Chief of Staff of the Visegrad tactical group at this time, am I right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it. Which paragraph did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's the second paragraph of the document before -- above the word "tasks."

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This had to do with the Chief of Staff of the corps and his agreement with the Visegrad tactical group commander. I didn't take part in that agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you not see the words "Chief of Staff" and "commander of Visegrad tactical group," Visegrad grad TG?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, but as the Chief of Staff it was up to me only to implement what the TG commander ordered me to do so. This obviously concerns the Chief of Staff of the SRK and the commander of the Visegrad TG.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Well my question was really simple. It was were you the Chief of Staff of the Visegrad TG at this time? The document is dated 1 April 1994.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under the heading of the document, in the subject line, it indicates that these are conclusions and tasks from a briefing at SRK command on 31 March 1994. Did you attend this briefing?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you attend any briefings at the SRK command before you -- before you joined the SRK?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I never attended it, and I was never present at any meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The tactical group commander was Dragisa Masal correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Colonel Dragisa Masal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And it says my reference wasn't complete. He was the commander of the Visegrad tactical group?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Would he attend meetings at the SRK command related to joint operations between the Drina Corps and the SRK?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. But what we just read states that it was as per agreement and request as arranged between the Visegrad TG commander and the Chief of Staff of the SRK. I don't know where they reached that arrangement, whether they were somewhere in the field or in Sarajevo. I was not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under item 8, it states: "Fortify positions around Sarajevo by erecting wire and concrete barriers which would in turn strengthen the belief that they really are blocked (in a camp)." Were you aware of these tasks which came from the SRK commander at that time when you joined later that year, in 1994? Did you become aware of this?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but "in a camp" is in quotation marks indicating that it wasn't a camp, at least that's what our grammar dictates.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, a more general question: Do you think that people kept inside wire and concrete barriers under the conditions where they would feel like they were really being blocked would feel like they were under siege?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What people?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, if there were positions that were fortified around Sarajevo by erecting wire and concrete barriers which would strengthen the belief that they are really blocked, wouldn't this create a feeling that people were under siege by the SRK? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm asking you what people you have in mind? Who was supposed to feel that way?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Those people inside the barriers. Whomever they are.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, these are actions and procedures aimed at persuading the enemy side, i.e. members of the 1st Corps of the ABiH, that they are under blockade. It is obvious and can be seen from here that no complete blockade was possible. It was just to create that impression with the enemy. That is the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I also ask -- yes. Could I ask one question. You emphasised that "in a camp" is in quotation marks and you explained that this means in your language that they were not in a camp, but I read that - and please correct me when you're language dictates otherwise - that as if they were in a camp, that that is what it means although not really being in a camp. That is how I understood it in the English translation. If you have any comment on it, please give it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are perfectly right. That was the point, to create the impression of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have heard sufficient evidence about Sarajevo to know that it's not strictly a camp. Please proceed. Yes, yes, Judge Moloto may have one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, you earlier said that this surrounding was surrounding the 1st Corps of the ABiH, but this paragraph 8 here says fortify positions around Sarajevo, and this is what Mr. Weber has been putting to you, that the surrounding was around Sarajevo, not just around the 1st Corps of the ABiH. Do you have any comment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, that's what it reads. But in soldierly parlance, we never discuss civilians. When we say Sarajevo, we have in mind the units of the enemy placed in Sarajevo. There is much confusion and imprecision but it's always meant the enemy side, the enemy forces; i.e., armed units and personnel. It does not include civilians. When we refer to personnel, we mean enemy soldiers, not the inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have heard evidence to the effect that units of the ABiH Army were within the civilian population of Sarajevo. How did you surround them and exclude surrounding the civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my statement, I say that the position of Serb settlements had been in existence for many centuries before the war. They were naturally located around the urban part of Sarajevo. Of course, there were Serbs in Sarajevo itself as well. When the war broke out, the inhabitants organised themselves to provide defence but it was around Sarajevo. That's where their homes were, that's where they lived. No one brought them in and no one came from elsewhere to surround Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I didn't suggest that they were brought in. I said how did you obviate surrounding civilians when you surrounded the army? I don't think what you said answers my question, but if you don't have an answer to my question, just say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I have an answer. Those who held their own civilians captive were supposed to free them rather than using them as a shield. They used their own people, their civilians, in the town itself as a shield in front of the forces of the 1st Corps. They are responsible for the plight of civilians in Sarajevo and not those who fought the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You're not answering my question. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could just ask one question before we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One question, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, is what you've just been answering to Judge Moloto basically what you put out in your propaganda during the war?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's the truth. What the gentleman asked me, it is mission impossible. How could anyone do that? To select in the city itself? Make a distinction between civilians and soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. Meanwhile, Mr. Ivetic, I'm addressing you when the witness leaves the courtroom. One of the other differences the Chamber notices in relation to what is found on transcript pages 18652 to 18654, that the statement we discussed at that time was a statement by a third person, that third person, perhaps to be called as a witness or not, but at least was not in court at that moment to answer any questions about the statement he had given. It was a third person. Now, does that change your position in any way?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It strengthens it, Your Honour. The statement that they're trying to admit here is the third person not in court. That's the bases of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought we were referring to this witness giving testimony in --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, I did not object to that document. I objected to the statement of Milan Lukic who is not in court and who is not giving evidence in this case, and therefore was the bases of my objection to that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're mixing a whole bunch of things up and I don't agree with that. And it's an Official Note of an interview with Milan Lukic from the Serbian DB, and if we -- you'd like submissions, we can make them at the proper time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I mixed it up. My apologies for that. We take a break and we will resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the Chamber -- Mr. Ivetic, we have looked at the transcript. Mr. Weber introduced 65 ter 30929 and said this was the trial record of your testimony in February 2002 before the high court. Now, a couple of pages later after we had dealt with that, we see that Mr. Weber said: "Q. We are going to go through some more documents. "MR. WEBER: But, Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 30932," which is still the same court record. And then -- under seal. And then you said: "Objection, Your Honour. During the Prosecution's case whenever we tried to use statements," et cetera. So we understood this in direct response to the tendering of the trial record known under number 65 ter 30392 but apparently you had something else in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I note the record now reflects three different numbers that you have said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if there is any need to correct the record if at that moment - and it's not about me, but it's about Mr. Weber saying that we are going to go through some more documents, but at this time the Prosecution tenders and then that number into evidence. If he has mentioned any others at that point in time, then we need a correction of the provisional transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this is actually becoming more confused. 30929 is the witness's -- is the trial record from the witness's previous testimony in 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I see that it's 932, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And then 30932 is a state security report from the Serbian DB. So I was using a separate document at that time, and my reference in the Serbian DB document I believe was to using even more documents along the lines of to further support what Milan Lukic had said in that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to sort that out. I was confused by the numbers now. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can clarify it by reminding Your Honours that with respect to this witness's prior testimony, my objection was that the entire answer was not being read into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the Milan Lukic interview, that is the one that I objected to under the grounds and the transcript reference that I cited of the other witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that now. I think we have misunderstood it. Apologies for that. And we'll further consider the objection and what was tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, if you're ready, you may continue. Apologies, Mr. Dragicevic for dealing with another matter when you entered the courtroom which is not very polite. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: A few minutes ago before the break, you said: "How could anyone do that? To select in the city itself? Make a distinction between civilians and soldiers?" Sir, as a senior commander in the SRK, is it your evidence that you believe it was not possible to distinguish between the civilians and soldiers in Sarajevo during your operations?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I said what I said. It is impossible if you are blocking a corps, which uses most of Sarajevo as its base, not to block the civilians who are being held captive by the very same 1st Corps of the ABiH. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, and the way in which you phrased the question is, of course, twisting the evidence of the witness. It was about blockades, not about any operations. And therefore, if you would put that to the witness, it should be clear that he's not confused because he was talking about a blockade and you are now saying are you saying that it was not possible to distinguish between civilians and -- during operations. Now, that's a different matter and you should have alerted the witness on the shift you made. Now, the witness happily enough was aware of it, apparently, but it was up to you, in all fairness to the witness, to have done that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Moving on, could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P361. And specifically could the Prosecution please have page 56 of the B/C/S original and page 46 of the English translation. I was looking for the original, if we could. I believe that there is a B/C/S transcription but there is also a handwritten original. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is an entry from General Mladic's notebooks dated 7 May 1994 related to an analysis of operation Zvijezda 94, or Star 94. We see in the text that it relates to a presentation that was held on this date which appears to have taken place in Srbinje. Were you present for this meeting, this presentation?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please go to page 60 of the B/C/S original and page 50 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention towards the bottom of the page. Before you are General Mladic's own notes about his own presentation given at this meeting. Toward the bottom of the page, the notes state: "We are not completely done with the M in the enclave of Gorazde. The enclave" --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if we could please have the next version in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "The enclave needs to be cut down, reduced, and made to suffer losses, especially on the outskirts, beyond a 3 KM perimeter. And in this way ensure there is no perspective for the survival of the M in this area." Do you agree that the notation M stands for Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Muslims under arms. This is primarily referred to, armed Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. You're interpreting that, right? It just says M.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if -- you said yourself that M stands for the Muslims, I'm just explaining that what is referred to is the Muslims, their armed men and units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. When -- when -- the statement in this way, ensure that that there is no perspective for the survival of the M in this area, isn't that referring to all Muslims in the area of Gorazde? Don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with you because all of us very often use the term "Muslims" but -- when meaning the "Muslim army." I do believe that this is what is referred to here. Muslims is Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were personally involved in these operations, to cut down and reduce the Gorazde enclave to the point where there was no perspective for Muslims in the area? I'm just putting it to you.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did take part to use combat operations to incapacitate the Muslim forces. Let's not forget that in 1992, Serbs who had lived there were en masse driven out of the territory of Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, let's stay focused on the matters at hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30937 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 7 April 1994 TG Visegrad order related to the Zvijezda 94 operation. Is it correct that this document is from you?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes. But it's the left hand part is not very legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I appreciate that. With that being noted I just wanted to ask you about some specific information that is legible. In the document, you ordered the transfer of guns to the Cabra area and tell the 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade to position them in a way that will allow them to directly fir eon the town. Can you see this information?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are to be positioned in the way that will allow them directly to fire, but when this term "grad," "town," refers to Muslim positions within the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, just please stay focused on my question. I'm going to go through the information. Where is the Cabra area?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is located on the left bank of the Drina and the left bank of the Praca, above Ustipraca which is an elevation above Ustipraca.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What town could be directly fired upon from this area?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not target any town. We targeted their positions along that axis. This is to do with the orientation of the guns towards their trenches and other fortifications which were located along the axis of our attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking for an explanation of the order. I'm just merely asking you what the order states. It says "in a way that will allow them to directly fire at the town." What town are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers to the positions in the town of Gorazde or, in other words, in the positions along the axis of Ustipraca and Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the town referred to here, and that was the question, Gorazde. That's clear. Could the witness also tell us what the reference to 1091 would mean? Does this number say anything to you, after the portion that is illegible?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Thank you, Mr. President. I erred. This does not refer to the town of Gorazde but to a fortification immediately before Gorazde, opposite Ustipraca. Now I was in two minds. I'm not sure that ZIS artillery cannot reach Gorazde from Cabra. A Cabra is a strong fortification called "grad." I presume that 1091 may refer to the number of the target. And this is illegible. I could not make out. But 1091 is the reference number of a target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a target list with those numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot claim decisively but we did determine the targets to be fired at. In my opinion this may refer to that. I cannot read the whole text. But this does not specifically refer to the town of Gorazde but to a hill which is named Grad. It can be seen from Ustipraca with the naked eye. It's semi- to the right in that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both parties are invited to provide whatever additional documentary evidence which would shed light on what 1091 may refer to. An elevation or a number on a target list, whatever. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders this document into evidence. It's 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Most probably this is an elevation, number of the elevation, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it should perhaps not be too difficult to find it for the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection to the tendering of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30937 receives number P6655, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Mr. Weber, any chance that you would finish within the next few minutes? So as to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just have one more document to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 30901.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a SRK command order dated 2 September 1995. It appears to be from you, correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not from the command of the SRK but from IKM and the number is illegible. I think it's IKM at 2 at Vogosca. That would be forward command post of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps where I was as commander of that forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this document at number 3, it says that Igman and Ilidza infantry brigades would prepare AB launchers which will be ready for taking over of military posts according to the Talus 1 -- I believe that that's a Talus 1 operation.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not military code but firing position, "vatrinja polozje [phoen]," firing position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. AB launchers from those positions. Then we see a little further down in the document that the Igman and Ilidza Brigade will prepare two FABs each of 250 and 105 kilogramme and load them on the vehicle of the Igman Infantry Brigade, and 3rd Sarajevo Infantry Brigade will also load. My question to you on this document is very simple. Is it correct that you issued orders related to the launching or preparations for the launching of modified air-bombs?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is my order, but it states here clearly on the basis of an order by the SRK commander. On the basis of that order I write my order addressed to the units which I currently command and that would be the IKM 2 Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30901 receives number P6656, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, yesterday at transcript page 23702 you were asked about your education and training in legal matters. Now I want to ask you, did you have people with legal training in the department to assist you with your work? And by "department" I mean the department for morale, religious affairs, and legal affairs within the SRK?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought he mentioned that yesterday, that he did have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I think it's also in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned an assistant for legal affairs, Captain Milenko Kuzmanovic. Was he a lawyer or legally trained?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he held a law degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now returning to your department's work at the SRK giving lectures on adherence to laws, international criminal law, who actually conducted the trainings? Was it you?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That would be my legal affairs assistant within the department. But also at brigade level we would have people with law degrees who would deal with legal affairs within brigades, within the section for morale, religious, and legal affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the reference to the international criminal law, where do I find that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The law of war it should be. The law of war it should be the reference. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said international criminal law, which is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can ask first for you to clarify, you said your legal affairs assistant within the department. Was that person trained as a -- trained in law?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he held a law degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to turn to your time spent in Visegrad. And we talked today about two volunteer platoons within the Visegrad Brigade. Why were they called volunteer platoons, sir?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those were people who resided outside the territory of the municipality of Visegrad or outside the Republika Srpska. They would come from Montenegro for the most part, Serbia, other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina, some from Russia. We called them that but they entered and were incorporated into companies as platoons or as individuals. These were not groups. These were platoons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can turn briefly to 65 ter number 30929, page 5 in both versions. It would be page 6 in the B/C/S and page 5 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You were asked earlier today about your prior testimony in the trial in relation to Mr. Ranisavljevic, and at that time you were asked about whether one of the smaller units from the Visegrad Brigade could carry out a military operation without you knowing about it. And in your answer, only the first line was read that said: "A unit could not carry out any military operation as a unit without my knowledge," and then your answer continued: "I again emphasise that none of the units could move about in the field without my knowledge because I would have to find out about it. However, individuals from the brigade who were given a furlough by a company commander for visiting their relatives to bathe and partake in other free time activities, the movements of these soldiers could not be followed, nor could I know where they were going. This was not my task and the brigade commander could not do this." Do you stand by this prior testimony from this trial as being truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is completely true. I commanded units, not individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could look at the answer to the next question, which is at the bottom of page 5 in English, and it will be on the same page in page 6 in the B/C/S, where you were asked whether volunteers from Serbia were assigned to the Visegrad Brigade, and your testimony is recorded as follows: "Volunteers coming from Serbia would report to the Visegrad MUP, Ministry of the Interior, and then to the military recruiting office, and they would then receive a summons for mobilisation by which they were assigned to the Visegrad Brigade thereby becoming an integral part of it. This was the case for the accused Nebojsa Ranisavljevic." Is this the procedure that you described earlier today when you mentioned the SJB and the recruitment office?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I can answer the question. It's exactly the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- he described, so therefore there is no need to ask it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. If we can call up 65 ter 02555.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record, it's number P6651 MFI'd, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this was the document shown to you by the Prosecution. The heading says "Command of the 1st Visegrad Light Infantry Brigade." Did such a command or such a formation ever exist, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, no. Maybe at the time of being set up, but I never heard of us being referred to. We were 1st Visegrad Brigade and then 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, but this is not the gist of it. What the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Understood?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- misuse of this certificate is the gist of the -- the crux of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have limited time. I'd like to try and get through everything so we can finish you today. Now you mentioned the absence of a date. Is anything else missing from the header of this document that you would expect to find from a legitimate document issued by the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that there is some leading aspect to that but there is also -- it's vague. There are many different types of documents issued by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. The witness may answer the question. Anything that strikes you as missing? That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, for such a document, this is a certificate. It's a common document. This form can stand. There may have been other details in the letter head but this certificate serves local purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were not asked about that. Is there anything that strikes you as missing compared to what you would expect for such a document? From your answer I take it that it's nothing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe the date below.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have paid attention to the date already.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you done with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No. No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We talked about the stamp earlier. I'd like to direct your attention to the number that is indicated in the stamp, number 1. What officer in the brigade would be assigned the number 1 stamp?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personnel officers. Personnel officers had custody of rubber stamps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall as chief of staff what the number of your stamp would have been?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm done with this document. If you have something further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question. The document is a double one, the one dealing with Milan Lukic, but there is another part which refers to Dragutin Dragicevic. To your knowledge is that person any way related to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, although I did have quite a lot of problems because of his surname being the same as mine. I don't believe that he was from Zvornik, not from Visegrad at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the answer is no, that is sufficient. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And following up on Your Honour's question, was Mr. Dragutin Dragicevic ever a member of the Visegrad Brigade?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if we could turn to Boban Indjic. During the time period you were at either the Visegrad Brigade, the Visegrad tactical group, or the 2nd Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade, did anyone ever report to you that Boban Indjic had been accused of committing a crime?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not only Boban Indjic but any other member of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to 65 ter number 02556.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record, this is Exhibit P6654, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is another document that the Prosecution showed to you. And earlier you wanted to point something out to us in this document about, I believe, the dates that are listed that Milan Lukic joined the brigade. Could you please complete your submission that you wanted to say? What is the significance of the date 26 April 1992?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 26th of April, at that time Visegrad Brigade did not exist. It was established 19th of May 1992. Therefore, he could not have been a member of that brigade. Of course, I stand by my statement that he was never a member of the Visegrad Brigade as long as I was in Visegrad either as commander, Chief of Staff of the brigade, and commander of the tactical group -- Chief of Staff of the tactical group.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever receive or see this document during the time period that you were at the Visegrad tactical group?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw it, and it can't be deduced from this document who is the addressee, who this document is addressed to for consideration or decision. There is no addressee of this document. There is no indication of who is this document addressed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters and the transcribers for the speed of my questioning, but I've completed my redirect. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Moloto has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, at page 82 lines 22 to 23 of today's transcript, you say -- sorry, let me just find it. You say you had quite a lot of problems because of this Dragutin Dragicevic having the same name as you. What kind of problems did you have?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By inertia everyone thought he was a cousin of mine because of his last name, and they wanted me to be able to provide some kind of protection due to that fact during the proceedings at the district court in Bijelo Polje and the high court in Belgrade. It came from the defence; that is to say, the counsel for the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you so much. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have the questions of the Bench triggered any need for further questions? If not, Mr. Dragicevic, I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties. But before I conclude, I told you that you would be given an opportunity at the end to add anything you thought we'd need to know directly related to any question put to you. If there is anything you'd like to add to that, so not general statements but anything that you said for a proper understanding of this and this answer to that and that question, you need to know A, B, or C, you have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I'd like to thank you. Second of all, it seems to me that I owe you a response to a question I did not hear yesterday. And I don't want to leave it without a reply if in any way able to do so so as to correct my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The only thing: You say I owe you a response to a question I did not hear yesterday. If that is a question which was not put to you, there is no need to reply to that. And I was a bit confused by you then saying, "And I don't want to leave it without a reply." But what question was it that you say you didn't hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You put it but I was unable to hear it, and I don't know what the question was at all. Maybe you can recall it. In any case, I'm just sorry for not having provided you with an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's appreciated that you're concerned about my questions being answered. I have no recollection of any questions which I've put to you to which I did not receive an answer such that I would invite you to answer that question now. So we will then leave it to that. Thank you again and I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 10th of July, in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 10th day of July, 2014, at 9.30 a.m.
